For Chey ♡

A little corner of the internet that belongs entirely to you.

I started this because I ran out of ways to tell you the same things in person without sounding like a broken record, so I figured I'd build you an entire website instead — which, in hindsight, is a much bigger commitment than just texting you more. But here we are. Everything on here is true, most of it is embarrassing for me to admit out loud, and all of it is about you.

♡
♡
page two

Your Heart

Before anything else — before the jokes, before the awards ceremony I built you two pages from now — I love your heart. This page is the sincere one. I'm not going to apologize for that.

I love your heart.

Not in the greeting-card way. In the specific way where you actually care about people, quietly, without needing credit for it. You check on people who aren't expecting to be checked on. You don't perform kindness — you just do it, and then you're on to the next thing like it wasn't a big deal, even when it was.

I love how you remember the little details.

I'll mention something once, off-hand, half-thinking you weren't even listening — and then weeks later you bring it up like it mattered. It always throws me off, in the best way. It's a small thing that makes me feel entirely understood.

I love how comfortable you make me feel.

I don't perform around you. I don't edit myself down to something more palatable. I can be ridiculous, or quiet, or in a mood I can't explain, and none of it scares you off. That's rarer than people think.

I love your honesty.

You tell me the truth, even the inconvenient versions of it. You don't manage me. I trust every word you say to me, which — if you knew me before you — is not something I hand out easily.

this page sounds like "The Middle" — Jimmy Eat World — the song about being fine, eventually, because someone's steady next to you.

page six

Us

Not what I love about you — what I love about the thing we've built together.

You show up. Not just for the good days. For the annoying, unglamorous, 2pm-on-a-Tuesday ones too. I don't think you realize how much that's worth.
You love loudly. Not in a dramatic way — in a "I will absolutely tell you and everyone else how much I like you" way. It's disarming, in a good way.
You're the one who plans us. The dates, the "let's do this thing" texts, the reservations. I love how much you actively want to build memories with me — it's never an afterthought with you.
It never feels like a chore to you. You get genuinely excited making plans for us, which somehow makes me excited too, even for things I'd normally never suggest myself.

    page nine, the last one

    If I Could Tell You One Thing

    I love your heart. I love your kindness, and the way it never asks to be noticed. I love how much you care — about the big things and the tiny ones I didn't think anyone would catch.

    I love your wit, and how smart you are, and how emotionally intelligent you are in a way I'm still learning from. I love how honest you are with me, and how safe that honesty makes me feel.

    I love your laugh, your smile, your voice. I love the way you light up the second something excites you. I love that you can be dead serious in one breath and completely unhinged in the next.

    I love how much you love me. I love how you plan our time together like it matters, because it does. I love how you remember the little things I say.

    But most importantly —

    I love you because you're you.

    Thank you for being my favorite person. ♡
